We already know he seeks truth, so that is satisfied regardless. But we need to decide if he can be non-academic in this branch. If he does NOT pursue learning and has life experience, is he forced to be scholarly minded? No direct rule forces it. He could value knowledge without being scholarly minded (the rule only gives seeking truth, which we already have). Thus in this branch he could choose non-academic. Hence it is possible for Raphael to be non-academic. Therefore the statement "Raphael is not non-academic" is not entailed; it is false in at least one consistent scenario.
